## Why visit

A strong reason to consider Rochdale: intimate traditional rooms, serious changing cask and a substantial food offer in the historic Toad Lane area. It sits beside the Rochdale Pioneers Museum, making a beer-and-local-history outing possible without a sprawling itinerary. The appeal is a complete, comfortable pub visit with time to eat and compare beers. Combine it with the Flying Horse for a manageable excursion, rather than adding several weaker stops simply to make a crawl. Cider is documented too, although the day’s choices should be checked.

## Beer

CAMRA documents seven changing real ales, plus continental draught and bottled options. CAMRA names Wakey Wakey Bright and Early and Serious Moonlight stout as regulars, alongside Pictish-brewed Lancashire Bitter house cask.

## Cider and perry

**Real cider documented; reconfirm stock.** CAMRA explicitly records real cider, sometimes on handpull; ask for the current list. CAMRA reports Seacider on handpump, but confirm the connected product qualifies and is currently pouring.

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

Official site provides a British main menu, sandwich menu and table booking. A good planned meal stop.

## Plan the visit

Reserve if the meal is central to the day. CAMRA’s single-number address and the official 33–37 address refer to the same Toad Lane venue.

**Getting there:** Toad Lane in central Rochdale; combine on foot with the Flying Horse.
